title: Sections over an affine open: vanishing at a point iff membership in its prime; basic opens are affine with ring the localization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an affine open, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and for $x\in U$ let $\mathfrak p_x\subset R$ be the prime ideal of $x$ given by $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $f\in R$ and $x\in U$ write $f(x)$ for the image of $f$ in the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $D(f)=\{x\in U: f(x)\neq0\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. Then: (a) for every $x\in U$, $f(x)=0$ in $\kappa(x)$ if and only if $f\in\mathfrak p_x$; equivalently, under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ the open $D(f)\subseteq U$ corresponds to $\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R: f\notin\mathfrak p\}$; (b) $D(f)$ is an affine open of $X$, and the restriction map $R=\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(D(f))$ is a localization of $R$ at the multiplicative set $\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$, i.e. induces an isomorphism $R_f\cong\mathcal O_X(D(f))$.

source.place: Schemes, proof of Lemma 26.12.4 (Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), the sentence 'f(t)=0 iff f in p' for (a); Lemma 26.5.6 (Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine) and Lemma 26.5.1 (Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves: O(D(f)) = R_f) for (b)
